policy_title: Introduce Rail Reform Bill to Create Great British Railways
stated: The Conservative Party will introduce a Rail Reform Bill in their first King’s Speech to create Great British Railways (GBR), headquartered in Derby, to deliver a revitalised private-public partnership, reliable services, simpler tickets, and growing the role of the private sector.

source.quote: We will introduce a Rail Reform Bill in our first King’s Speech to create Great British Railways (GBR), headquartered in Derby. GBR will usher in a revitalised private-public partnership, delivering a modern and innovative railway with reliable services, and simpler tickets.

bearing_set.reason: 'Simpler tickets' is a concrete stated commitment that directly bears on the affordability and cost of rail for millions of commuters, a real household expenditure; pricing structure reform could materially raise or lower effective fares.
'Growing the role of the private sector' is a structural lever that directly bears on rail workers' terms, job security, and conditions — historically a contested trade-off in UK rail reform.

Reliable rail services and improved network integration directly affect business connectivity, labour mobility, and regional economic opportunity — core O13 indicators of productivity and living standards.

membership_note: Three genuine bearings: the prosperity/connectivity effect (O13, the designed-for outcome), the fare-accessibility effect on household costs (O2), and the labour-conditions effect of private sector expansion (O4, the adversarial tradeoff). O12 is plausible but too vague at this stage — no funding envelope or subsidy commitment is stated, so the fiscal effect cannot be pinned to a specific indicator.
